title: Margin
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: The engine already puts MCP server tools behind ToolSearch by its own rule (ToolDescribeInput.isDeferred doc), so the dead weight it promises to remove is mostly gone already, and ToolInfo carries no schema so the sizes it would show are guesses.
stamps.subject: Attic

stamps.reason: Attributing listeners by a port snapshot before and after every Bash call spawns a process per call, misses servers that bind after the call returns, and ends in a kill button on a guessed pid: cost and risk out of proportion to an occasional port-in-use message.
stamps.subject: Strays

stamps.reason: A variation on what exists: vows-widget and stakes-widget already stop a matched command at the permission step with a reason, and notes-widget and capsule-widget already hold the person's reminder text.
stamps.subject: Tripwire

stamps.reason: A variation on situation-widget and the built-in @ mention: it sends the same last-error and last-file facts with the prompt, only on a typed keyword, and needs a timer polling the prompt box to preview them.
stamps.subject: Shorthand

stamps.reason: The longest deleted run is most often a mistaken paste, which can be a secret put back on screen, and the softened or sharpened tally is word-list guesswork, so the promised moment is rare and the common one is noise or exposure.
stamps.subject: Unsaid

stamps.reason: It depends on a raw thinking stream that is often off or summarised, and matching 'actually' and 'wait' at sentence starts gives a count nobody can trust, so most sessions would show the empty state or noise.
stamps.subject: Second Thoughts

stamps.reason: A phrase counter with a picture is a variation on the reactive scenes and badges, and it rests on a short list of stock phrases that current models seldom say, so the jar would sit empty.
stamps.subject: The Jar

stamps.reason: Not chosen: it survives on novelty, but the Image element draws pixels only in kitty and Ghostty, so on most terminals, including Windows Terminal and tmux, and on the demo page, the card is a file name; Margin works wherever fullscreen does.
stamps.subject: Lightbox

stamps.reason: Margin is the only idea that gives the person a new way to act: annotate passages of Claude's reply by mouse selection and send them back as one quoted prompt, using ui.selection and Input which no widget has touched, at no token cost, on any terminal in fullscreen.

No blocking fault: every call and type is in this build's types, all main states and the 20-column card are drawn, the spec is at 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 11 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

Two acceptance clauses cannot be proven the way the spec says, in this build's test kit: (1) A1/A2/A5 want ui.focus calls recorded through ground() answers or a bottom hook, but $.ui.focus rejects with 'no implementation for ui.focus' before any hook or answer is reached, so neither 'once with the press's requestId and key remark' nor 'not at all in below' nor a deny can be observed, only that the card is the same after the rejection; (2) A8 wants a fill answering { isFilled: false, refusal: 'dialog' }, but the engine strips a refusal a hook writes, so the widget only ever sees { isFilled: false } and 'A dialog is open. Marks kept.' is unreachable in a test. Reword A2 and A8 (move both to the Live hand check) and the widget, which is built and passes the checker with the rest of A1-A15 tested, needs no code change.

Both send-back faults are fixed (the ui.focus recording and the dialog refusal moved from A1, A2, A5 and A8 to the Live hand check) and no blocking fault is in what changed, at 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 14 notes in spec-notes.md, 3 of them new.

Margin widget built to the revised spec: mouse-selected passages marked with remarks and appended to the prompt box as quotes, all 15 acceptance lines tested and the checker passing; the ui.focus call and the dialog sentence are kept in register.tsx as hand checks.

The checker fails about every other run: test A5 times out (4.97 to 5.14 s against the 5 s limit, FAIL/PASS/FAIL/PASS over four runs), so make A5 (and A7 at 4.26 s) finish well under the limit without losing a clause and pass the checker five times in a row; also answer spec notes 2, 5 and 14 in the build notes (field in below, slash commands reaching prompt.submit, hand checks not observed). Code, live run and store are otherwise to spec; see inspection.md.

Margin tests rewritten to hold one mounted card per test and read it with drawn(), so A5 mounts once instead of about forty times and every clause is kept in one test; the checker passed five times in a row, twice over. Build notes. Note 2 (field in below): not observed, no fullscreen session was run; by the types only Pane and AbovePrompt keep a focus ring (UiFocusComponent), so the remark field in the below placement may never take the keys; the field is still drawn there because A2 and A15 ask for the same card in all three placements, and mark <remark> is the way round it. Note 5 (slash commands and prompt.submit): not observed; the types give command.run and prompt.submit as separate events and the test engine raises no prompt.submit for a command, but the headless live run cannot hold a mark to show it, so no guard and no command-shaped prompt were added; if a typed command does reach prompt.submit as composer, /margin-widget drop 1 after a send would wipe the marks first and the hook needs a guard. Note 14 (hand checks): none of the four was observed by the machinist: the field taking keys after Mark, the mark verb seeing the selection, ui.focus moving the keys in side and above (with below right without it and a deny leaving the card as it was), and Send under an open dialog showing the dialog sentence; all four are left for the director in a fullscreen terminal.

Checker passes five times in a row (A5 down from 5.0 s to 3.5 s with every clause kept), code, tests, live run and store are to spec and the build notes are answered; the mouse path in a fullscreen terminal is still unobserved and its hand checks are owed by the director, see inspection.md findings 1 and 2.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
